title: Interoperable and explainable machine learning models to predict morbidity and mortality in acute neurological injury in the pediatric intensive care unit: secondary analysis of the TOPICC study
summary: In a TOPICC secondary analysis of 1,860 pediatric intensive-care patients flagged for possible acute neurological injury, an ensemble of machine-learning models improved mortality precision measures over the original logistic model. The work concerns retrospective risk prediction and does not establish that using the models improves care.
ai_technology: An ensemble meta-regressor combines random forest, gradient boosting, and SVM on admission physiology; SHAP ranks contributing predictors.
organization: University of Utah; Intermountain Primary Children’s Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Out-of-bag assessment reported mortality AUROC 0.91 and average precision 0.59 versus 0.49 for the original model; at specificity 0.995, PPV was 0.79 versus 0.60.
evidence.unknown: Secondary retrospective analysis with internal resampling; no prospective decision impact or patient benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: An ensemble meta-regressor combines random forest, gradient boosting, and SVM on admission physiology; SHAP ranks contributing predictors.
